title.narrative: Strengthening the foundations of a System to Account for Syria’s Missing Persons

description.narrative: Throughout the implementation period, the project contributed to laying the groundwork for the establishment of a future Syrian state that secures the rights of all surviving families of the missing and survivors of enforced disappearance, including women, to justice, truth and reparation. This entails progress in the development of a secure, impartial, and independent data repository and in strengthening the capacities of Syrian civil society organizations and families of the missing, thus enabling them to become active advocates for a law-based approach to accounting for Syria’s missing.

title.narrative: Output 1.3: Capacity of first responders and other stakeholders operating in Syria to safeguard forensic evidence for future accountability purposes is improved
Trainings conducted for CSOs and other stakeholders on the process of protecting forensic sites and human remains.

comment.narrative: Baseline: February 2020 16 CSOs and activists out of which 3 were women(43%- the baseline used here is a result of one simulation event completed in the Hague under the previous UK CSSF funding)
60 CSO representatives and families, out of which at least 14 are women, have increased awareness about safe-guarding principles : 60%, March 2023 (awareness events)

40 representatives of civil society organizations and 27 lawyers, activists, and relatives of missing persons. In total 67 participants, including 30 women, have increased awarness about safeguarding principles: 100% reported that their knowledge in the process of safeguarding is improved because of ICMP’s intervention. Participants demonstrated an average of 39% increase in knowledge at the end of the trainings.

title.narrative: Output Indicator 1.3 (a): % of first responders, and other stakeholders directly involved in the excavations, disaggregated by gender, reporting that their knowledge in the process of safeguarding for the missing is improved because of ICMP’s intervention.

description.narrative: The project achieved the following results, which contributed to building the capacity of first responders and other stakeholders operating in Syria to safeguard forensic evidence for future accountability purposes: - The knowledge of 67 representatives (30 women) of CSOs based in northeast Syria as well as activists and relatives of missing persons of the process of protecting forensic sites and human remains increased;- The knowledge of 45 representatives (10 women) of stakeholders involved in mass grave excavations, including forensic medicine practitioners, of safeguarding forensic evidence for future accountability purposes increased.
